bib.title: ConvNeXt V2: Co-designing and Scaling ConvNets with Masked Autoencoders

legacy_report:
SOURCE: ConvNeXt V2: Co-designing and Scaling ConvNets with Masked Autoencoders. Woo, Debnath, Hu, Chen, Liu, Kweon, Xie. The PDF is arXiv:2301.00808v1 (2 Jan 2023) and prints no venue; "CVPR 2023" comes only from the note and references.md, so I could not confirm it here.

COVERAGE: 69,051 of 69,051 chars, all 15 pages, including appendices and tables. References were read for origins. Nothing skipped.

Quotes keep the extraction's line-break hyphens. Page offsets: p1 0, p3 9633, p4 14680, p5 18027, p6 22769, p7 26866, p8 32003, p9 37137, p10 41688, p11 45770, p12 49875, p13 53933.

CLAIMS

- claim: The headline range mixes setups. Atto is an IN-1K result; Huge 88.9% uses IN-22K labels and larger images.
  number: 76.7% (3.7M) to 88.9% (650M)
  setup: 76.7 is FCMAE then IN-1K fine-tuning, 224 single crop (Table 14). 88.9 is FCMAE, then IN-22K fine-tuning, then IN-1K fine-tuning, at 512² (Table 5/15).
  quote: "a 650M Huge model that reaches a state-of-the-art 88.9% accuracy when using IN-22K labels"
  where: p2

- claim: On IN-1K alone at 224, Huge reaches 86.3, below MAE ViT-H at 86.9.
  number: 86.3 vs 86.9
  setup: IN-1K pre-training, end-to-end fine-tuning, 224 px, 1600 pre-training epochs.
  quote: "ConvNeXt V2-H FCMAE 659M 1600 86.3" and "ViT-H MAE 632M 1600 86.9"
  where: p7, Table 4

- claim: The 88.9 "state of the art" margin is 0.1 over MViTV2-H, and it holds only among public-data methods.
  number: 88.9 vs 88.8
  setup: IN-1K validation, 512²; comparators trained with IN-22K supervised labels; no seeds or error bars reported.
  quote: "ConvNeXt V2-H 5122 659M 600.7G 88.9" and "MViTV2-H 512 2 667M 763.5G 88.8"
  where: p8, Table 5

- claim: FCMAE alone gives no gain over supervised training; GRN plus FCMAE does.
  number: 83.8 (V1 sup), 83.7 (V1 FCMAE), 84.3 (V2 sup), 84.6 (V2 FCMAE)
  setup: ConvNeXt-Base, IN-1K; FCMAE pre-trains 800 epochs and fine-tunes 100; supervised baseline 300 epochs.
  quote: "V1 + Sup, 300ep. V1 + FCMAE V2 + FCMAE / 83.8 83.7 84.6"; "ConvNeXt V2-B Supervised 89M 15.4G 84.3 ( +0.5)"
  where: p6, p7 Table 3

- claim: The co-design gain grows with model size, at Large versus Base.
  number: +1.3 Large, +0.8 Base
  setup: 800-epoch FCMAE, fine-tuned, relative to V1 supervised.
  quote: "ConvNeXt V2-L FCMAE 198M 34.4G 85.6 (+1.3)"
  where: p7, Table 3

- claim: Blocking leakage with sparse convolution is essential.
  number: 79.3 without, 83.7 with
  setup: ConvNeXt-Base, V1 block (no GRN), FCMAE on IN-1K, 800 pre-training and 100 fine-tuning epochs.
  quote: "w/o Sparse conv. w/ Sparse conv. / 79.3 83.7"
  where: p3

- claim: GRN must be present in both pre-training and fine-tuning.
  number: 78.8 dropped at fine-tuning, 80.6 added only at fine-tuning, 84.6 both
  setup: ConvNeXt-Base, IN-1K fine-tuning.
  quote: "drop at ft. 78.8 / add at ft. 80.6 / both 84.6"
  where: p6, Table 2f

- claim: GRN beats other normalisers and matches gating layers without their added parameters.
  number: GRN 84.6 at 89M; LRN 83.2, BN 80.5, LN 83.8; SE 84.4 and CBAM 84.5 at 109M
  setup: ConvNeXt-Base, IN-1K fine-tuning.
  quote: "BN [41] 80.5"; "SE [37] 84.4 109M"; "GRN 84.6 89M"
  where: p6, Table 2d-e

- claim: FCMAE masks less than MAE's 75%, and 0.6 was the best ratio tested.
  number: 0.6; 32×32 patches; best range 0.5-0.7
  setup: Mask size 32×32, IN-1K accuracy (Figure 8).
  quote: "we randomly remove 60% of the 32× 32 patches"; "a masking ratio in the range of 0.5 to 0.7 produces the best results"
  where: p3, p13

- claim: A single ConvNeXt block decoder ties the UNet and is faster.
  number: 83.7 at 7.7 hours vs 12.9 hours; 1.7× speedup
  setup: ConvNeXt-Base, 800 pre-training epochs, 256-core TPU-v3 pod using JAX; speedup relative to the UNet baseline.
  quote: "ConvNeXt block 83.7 7.7 1.7×"; "UNet w/ skip 83.7 12.9 -"
  where: p4, Table 1a

- claim: Sparse encoding's efficiency gain is a moderate byproduct, measured against dense masked convolution.
  number: 1.3× throughput, 2× lower max memory
  setup: 224×224, ratio 0.6, batch 64 per GPU, MinkowskiEngine, PyTorch, RTX A6000; simulated masked input, 20 steps.
  quote: "a moderate increase in pre-training efﬁciency, with an average of 1.3× increase in throughput and a 2× decrease in max memory usage"
  where: p12

- claim: COCO box AP improves with both proposals and beats Swin + SimMIM at each size.
  number: Huge 55.7 vs 54.4; Base 52.9 vs 52.3; V1-B supervised 50.3
  setup: Mask R-CNN, 3x schedule, single-scale test with soft-NMS, COCO val2017, IN-1K pre-trained initialisation.
  quote: "ConvNeXt V2-H FCMAE 2525G 55.7 75.2 61.8 48.9 72.8 53.6"; "Swin V2-H SimMIM − 54.4"
  where: p8, Table 6

- claim: On ADE20K, V2 loses to Swin at Base and wins at Large and Huge; the paper calls Base and Large "on par".
  number: Base 52.1 vs 52.8; Large 53.7 vs 53.5; Huge 55.0 vs 54.2; 57.0 with 22K
  setup: UperNet, 160K iterations, multi-scale test, initialised from weights after supervised IN-1K fine-tuning.
  quote: "Swin-B SimMIM 512 2 52.8 121M 1181G"; "ConvNeXt V2-B FCMAE 5122 52.1 122M 1170G"
  where: p8, Table 7; p10

- claim: FCMAE beats MoCo v3 on fine-tuning with the same encoder.
  number: 84.9 vs 83.7 (supervised 84.3)
  setup: ConvNeXt V2-Base, default recipes for each method; supervised is 300 epochs.
  quote: "Sup, 300ep. MoCo V3 FCMAE / 84.3 83.7 84.9"
  where: p13

- claim: V2 has more class-generic late-layer features, which the authors link to transfer, while deferring more exploration.
  number: none
  setup: Class selectivity index on the IN-1K validation set, V1 and V2 FCMAE weights.
  quote: "We leave more explorations as a future study."
  where: p12

LIMITS
- Only end-to-end fine-tuning is evaluated: "we focus on the end-to-end ﬁne-tuning performance" (p3). There are no linear-probe or frozen-feature results for FCMAE.
- Feature collapse is called a "potential issue" (p2) and rests on visualisations plus cosine distance on 1,000 validation images. It is "mainly observed" in dimension-expansion MLP layers. The link from diversity to accuracy is inferred, not separately tested.
- The authors concede Huge "slightly lagged" ViT on IN-1K and offer only speculation about why ("might be", p7).
- The main results ran on TPU with dense masked convolution, not sparse convolution; the authors state the outputs are numerically identical (p9). Sparse libraries "are not highly optimized for modern hardware" (p11).
- ADE20K initialises from supervised fine-tuned weights, because raw self-supervised weights performed worse (p10).
- No seeds, variance or significance are reported, while many comparisons differ by 0.1-0.3. Competitor numbers partly come from other papers ("Swins' results are from [77]"), so they are not same-run comparisons.
- "State-of-the-art" is dated to January 2023 and restricted to public data.

BUILDS ON
- ConvNeXt: Liu et al., 2022 [52].
- MAE: He et al., 2022 [31].
- BEiT: Bao et al., 2022 [3].
- SimMIM: Xie et al., 2022 [77].
- Submanifold sparse convolution: Graham and van der Maaten, 2017 [28]; Graham et al., 2018 [27].
- Minkowski engine: Choy et al., 2019 [15].
- PointContrast: Xie et al., 2020 [76].
- Response normalisation: Krizhevsky et al., 2017 [45].
- Lateral inhibition: Hartline et al., 1956 [30]; Campbell and Robson, 1968 [6].
- SE: Hu et al., 2018 [37]. CBAM: Woo et al., 2018 [72]. LayerScale: Touvron et al., 2021 [65].
- Small variants: Wightman, 2019 [70].
- Masked ConvNet difficulty: Jing et al., 2022 [43].

CODE (Algorithm 1, p5). The code divides by the channel mean while Eq. 2 divides by the sum; footnote 1 reconciles them by scaling by channel count C.
```
gx = torch.norm(X, p=2, dim=(1,2), keepdim=True)
nx = gx / (gx.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)+1e-6)
return gamma * (X * nx) + beta + X
```

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p1, model scaling: shows the per-size gain at a glance, up to 86 on the axis, so it excludes the 88.9 result.
- Fig 2, p3, FCMAE framework: the sparse encoder, decoder and masked-only loss in one picture.
- Fig 3, p4, feature activation visualisation: makes dead or saturated channels visible, V1 against V2.
- Fig 4, p5, feature cosine distance: shows collapse across layers for V1, V2, supervised and MAE ViT.
- Fig 5, p6, block designs: exactly where GRN goes and LayerScale leaves.
- Fig 8, p13, masking ratio: the curve behind 0.6.
- Lower priority: Fig 6, p11 (sparse encoding efficiency); Fig 7, p12 (class selectivity).

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions. Extraction is clean apart from flattened superscripts ("5122" means 512²) and scrambled equations.
- Source inconsistencies:
  - Huge is 650M (abstract, p2, p7), 659M (Fig 1, Tables 4-5, A.1) and 660M (Tables 14-15).
  - The Table 5 caption says "IN-21K labels" while the text says ImageNet-22K.
  - The Table 15 caption says 224 crop but lists 384 and 512 rows.
  - Appendix D expands GRN as "Global Relation Network".
  - Table 14 V2-B and V2-L FCMAE (84.9, 85.8) match the 1600-epoch rows of Table 4, while Table 3 uses 800-epoch (84.6, 85.6). Table 14 states no epochs, so this pairing is my inference.

COMPARISON WITH THE NOTE
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/data-science/02-deep-learning/notes/04-convolutional-networks.md, line 196 (also frontmatter line 15). The grep confirms the citation. Line 196 is the only ConvNeXt mention in the note. References row: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/data-science/02-deep-learning/references.md:46.

The numbers themselves are correct: 76.7, 3.7M, 88.9 and 650M all match the abstract. The problems are setup and framing.

1. MISSING SETUP, most important. "Reported top-1 on ImageNet runs from 76.7% with a 3.7M Atto model to 88.9% with a 650M Huge." This reads as one scale under one protocol, but it is not (first claim above). The same-protocol range is 76.7 to 86.3 (IN-1K only, 224). This also breaks the repo rule that every number carries its setup.

2. MISLEADING JUXTAPOSITION. The preceding sentences give MAE ViT-H "on ImageNet alone" 87.8% at 448 px. A reader will conclude 88.9 beats it. But V2's 88.9 uses IN-22K labels at 512², which is exactly the condition the MAE sentence excludes. On the same footing in this paper's Table 4, ViT-H MAE wins, 86.9 to 86.3. The note never says this, and the authors concede it. The 87.8 itself was not checked against this source, which reports MAE only at 224 (86.9).

3. UNDER-QUALIFIED. "Counters feature collapse" states as settled what the paper calls a "potential issue". Its evidence is visualisations and a cosine-distance analysis on 1,000 images, in a FCMAE-trained ConvNeXt-Base. The definition also drops "saturated" ("dead or saturated feature maps") and that the behaviour is mainly in the dimension-expansion MLP layers. Minor.

4. MISSING: no number shows that either component matters, although the note gives such numbers for BEiT and MAE. Candidates: V1 FCMAE 83.7 vs V1 supervised 83.8 vs V2 FCMAE 84.6 (ConvNeXt-Base); sparse convolution 79.3 vs 83.7. The note also omits the paper's central finding, that FCMAE without GRN does not beat supervised training.

5. MISSING CAVEAT, frozen features. The note reports linear-probe weakness for BEiT and MAE, then says nothing for V2. The paper has no frozen-feature evaluation, so the silence could read as the problem being absent. "Tests only fine-tuning" would close this.

6. MISSING SETUP, masking ratio. MAE's 75% is stated right before V2, and V2's 60% of 32×32 patches is not, so a reader may carry over 75%.

7. IMPLIED EFFICIENCY. The note gives MAE's 3.3× compute saving and then says V2 "uses sparse convolutions". A reader may assume a similar saving, or that the numbers came from sparse hardware runs. The paper reports a moderate 1.3× throughput and 2× memory gain, against masked dense convolution, on GPU. The main results used masked dense convolution on TPU (numerically identical per the authors). The note's stated purpose, preventing leakage, is correct and matches the paper's "primary purpose". Sparse convolution applies only during pre-training and converts back to dense at fine-tuning.

8. MINOR.
   - "3.7M" and "650M" do not say parameters.
   - "ImageNet" should be ImageNet-1K validation.
   - Huge is 659M in the tables; 650M is the abstract's rounding.
   - "CVPR 2023" is not verifiable from this PDF.
   - The note jumps to V2 without ever introducing ConvNeXt V1, so "V2" has no antecedent.

Supported as written: fully convolutional masked autoencoder; sparse convolutions to stop leakage; GRN as a new layer; the "borrowed from vision transformers" framing. Table 4 also lists ViT-B BEiT at 83.2 (800 epochs), consistent with the note's BEiT figure.

Ledger: scripts/papers/ledger.jsonl:838 shows status "downloaded" and topic "classical-ml" for this paper, though the note already cites it. I report that without judging it.
